newsitem.title: INDIA: India set to buy one mln tonnes of crude from Iraq.
newsitem.headline: India set to buy one mln tonnes of crude from Iraq.

text.p: India's state-owned Indian Oil Corp has been given a mandate to import up to one million tonnes of crude oil from Iraq under the U.N.-supervised "oil-for-food" programme, an official said on Friday.

"Once the United Nations permits the second sale of crude oil under the oil-for-food programme, a delegation comprising IOC and ministry officials would head for Iraq to contract the purchase," the senior Petroleum Ministry official told Reuters by telephone.
The actual quantity contracted from Iraq and the price per barrel of crude oil purchased would depend on what the UN permits, he said.

During 1996/97 ending March 31 the IOC was given permission to import up to 500,000 tonnes of Iraqi crude under the first phase of the $2.0 billion oil-for-food programme but the contracted volumes were lower because India was a late entrant in the negotiations, the Petroleum Ministry official said.
An official of the government's Oil Coordination Committee said that the volume supplied last year was 50,000 tonnes at a price of $19 per barrel.
The official said the new oil-for-food package with Iraq was yet to be completed since Iraq was still negotiating with the United Nations for relaxation of some conditions.
Earlier on Friday India's state-run Tea Board said in a statement that the private-sector Tata Tea had secured a contract to export 1,000 tonnes of black tea to Iraq under the oil-for-food programme.
The statement did not specify how much Iraqi crude oil India would receive as part of the tea export deal.

Iraq is expected to more than double its oil exports next month to around 1.5 million barrels per day (bpd) to make up for a gap between the end of the first oil-for-food deal and the beginning of the second.

The second deal began on June 8 but Iraq has delayed exporting oil for two months and will now have to sell oil at a much higher rate in August than previously reckoned, or forego some of its oil sales under the scheme.
The United Nations confirmed late on Wednesday that Iraq must sell around $1.0 billion worth of oil by early September under the renewed oil-for-food deal.
